title: Perfect constant coefficients invert one normalized derived diagram projection
statement:
Let A be a commutative ring with an adic coefficient datum d [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], including perfectness of every A/I^(m+1) and finiteness of those quotients. Let f:U→V be any morphism of schemes. Work with the original small pro-etale sites (objects in universe t+1, morphisms in t), their constant A-module categories and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix n≥0. Put E_X(M)=Res_{A→d.finiteRing(X,n)}(d.finiteRing(X,n)⊗_A M), using the canonical constant-to-finite quotient map.
Let F_V and F_U be any additive functors from their module categories to strict inverse A-module diagrams. Let D_V and D_U be universal left-derived model data for these functors, computed on all K-flat complexes [def-weil-pbc-derived-reduction-model-data, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Specify an ordinary isomorphism e:F_V f^*_{diag}≅f^* F_U and a derived isomorphism τ:R_V G_f≅f^*R_U. Require its complex-counit normalization PullNormalized: for every K-flat complex P, τ at QP followed by the pullback factor and the U complex counit equals the diagram pullback of the V complex counit followed by its exact-functor factor and Q(e_P).
Specify isomorphisms e_V:ev_n F_V≅E_V and e_U:ev_n F_U≅E_U. Require the evaluated ordinary square to agree, under these isomorphisms, with the canonical scalar/pullback comparison formed by restriction/pullback and the inverse of its scalar-extension mate. In formulas, for every ordinary module M,
ev_n(e_M) followed by e_U(f^*M) equals f^*(e_V(M)) followed by the canonical quotient balancing comparison. The scalar-extension mate is assumed invertible (the ordinary pullback theorem supplies this); no hypothesis concerns other indices.
For every K∈D(U,A), define π_K:R_V(Rf_*K)→R^diag f_*R_U K as the adjunct of τ_{Rf_*K} followed by R_U of the ambient derived counit. Then ev_n(π_K) is invertible in D(V,A). There is no boundedness, properness, constructibility, completeness or etale-origin condition on K or f. This theorem is at one fixed finite coefficient; joint conservativity of all evaluations is a separate argument.

proof.text: For the specified index n, choose a bounded finite-projective A-complex representing A/I^(n+1), using the perfect-quotient field of the adic datum. Apply the exact commutative constant-module functor on each original small pro-etale site. It preserves the quasi-isomorphism and the explicit retractions of finite free terms. The canonical finite coefficient sheaf comparison identifies its derived value with the finite residue sheaf used by scalarLevel. This includes the zero ring, rank zero, I=A and n=0 (which means exponent one).

proof.text: Evaluate the two universal model counits at n. They are invertible on K-flat representatives. Their complex counits and the specified eV/eU comparisons therefore identify the evaluated derived functors with derived tensor by the preceding perfect constant coefficient. Compute on flat-term K-flat resolutions. The ordinary balancing square he, followed by PullNormalized, identifies the evaluated derived pullback comparison with canonical coefficient balancing. Descent through the localization of resolving complexes makes this identification natural and independent of the resolution. Other indices and transitions are not used.

proof.text: A K-injective strict tower evaluates to a K-injective complex, since evaluation has an exact left adjoint. Under the canonical evaluation/direct-image comparison, the fraction characterization of the derived adjunction identifies evaluation of the tower counit with the ordinary derived counit. Thus evaluating the displayed projection gives the counit-tensor projection for the fixed coefficient, conjugated by the model comparisons of the previous step. This is an identification of the specified map, not just of its endpoints.

source.place: Tags 0B56 (the counit-tensor projection), 0944 (perfect coefficient argument), and 0941 (derived evaluation of strict diagrams); original-site specialization of completion-mate-comparison proof Step 3.

proof.text: Compute this perfect-coefficient projection on a K-injective representative of K. For a finite free term its inverse is the finite-product comparison for the right adjoint; for a finite-projective term insert its inclusion and retraction into a finite free term. The ordinary tensor-adjunction total maps and their inverse equations are the abstract, independent-universe construction in ProjectionFormulaArrows. Boundedness of the coefficient makes each diagonal sum finite, even for unbounded K. The signs in both composites coincide on every summand. Localize the chain inverse equations, using the derived adjunction normalization to identify the forward map with the counit-tensor adjunct. Conjugation by the preceding comparisons proves invertibility of the single evaluated projection. No joint conservativity or faithfulness of evaluations is used in this lemma.

proof_origin.note: Extracts the genuine one-coefficient perfect projection argument from the parent. The generic equal-object/hom-universe totalization theorem does not directly instantiate on the original pro-etale site. The existing abstract tensor-adjunction total maps have independent category universes and give the intended chain calculation. The parent supplies ordinary balancing and the normalized derived comparison, then proves joint conservativity separately; it does not assume the desired tower isomorphism.

theorem evaluation_isIso (n : ℕ) [IsIso (scalarPullInv d f n)]
    (hτ : PullNormalized FV FU
      (proEtaleRingModulePullback f (exchangeConstantRing V A) (exchangeConstantRing U A)
        (exchangeConstantIso f A))
      (exchangeTowerModulePull f (exchangeConstantRing V A) (exchangeConstantRing U A)
        (exchangeConstantIso f A)) DV DU e τ)
    (eV : FV ⋙ (CategoryTheory.evaluation ℕᵒᵖ (proEtaleRingModules V
      (exchangeConstantRing V A))).obj (op n) ≅ scalarLevel d V n)
    (eU : FU ⋙ (CategoryTheory.evaluation ℕᵒᵖ (proEtaleRingModules U
      (exchangeConstantRing U A))).obj (op n) ≅ scalarLevel d U n)
    (he : ∀ M : proEtaleRingModules V (exchangeConstantRing V A),
      (e.hom.app M).app (op n) ≫
          eU.hom.app ((proEtaleRingModulePullback f (exchangeConstantRing V A)
            (exchangeConstantRing U A) (exchangeConstantIso f A)).obj M) =
        (proEtaleRingModulePullback f (exchangeConstantRing V A) (exchangeConstantRing U A)
          (exchangeConstantIso f A)).map (eV.hom.app M) ≫
            (ordinaryComparison d f n).hom.app M)
    (K : reductionDerivedCategory U (exchangeConstantRing U A)) :
    IsIso (((CategoryTheory.evaluation ℕᵒᵖ (proEtaleRingModules V (exchangeConstantRing V A))).obj
      (op n)).mapDerivedCategory.map (projection f FV FU DV DU τ K))
